PC: Demonstrated Physical presence at bedside <= 5 min
Obtained pertinent history in 5 min or less
Asks about time of symptom onset
Asks for finger stick glucose value
Asks about risk factors in the PMH (relevant history of diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, history of previous strokes etc.)
Requests appropriate labs (CBC, BMP, Troponin, INR) immediately
Asks about contraindications to tPA when talking to family member

Orders TPA 0.9 mg/kg and gives the following instructions for dosing:

10% in 10 minutes

90% over 50 minutes
MK: Reviews CT. Can also be done by phone call/written report, etc. by neuroradiologist. CTA optional for institutions who have capabilities of either in house access to interventional vascular services or can timely transfer to such.
SBP: Discussion with endovascular team( if applicable
Requests ICU bed and determines code status. Consider Stepdown or Stroke unit bed depending upon institutional protocol.
ICS:
Consents family member/patient (if patient is aphasic), specifically mentioning the following:

Risks: bleed 3-6%, risk of allergic reaction

Benign: 1/3 improvement of outcomes

Alternate: do nothing, support

Delegates effectively to team members:

* Data collection
* Collateral history
* Verification of time of symptom onset
* Consenting of patient or if needed a surrogate decision maker
